result.title: Twice as Fast, Until It Isn't: Quantized Serving of Mid-Size Open LLMs
result.summary: A team serving a 9B-20B open-weight language model on vLLM or SGLang must choose a quantization recipe, and needs two numbers: the speedup over BF16 and the accuracy given up. We assemble every public measurement of these numbers that we could verify and find that the record supplies them only in pieces. Only two checkpoints, both INT4 builds of Gemma 3 12B, have both a vLLM timing and an accuracy score, and that score covers a single MMLU subject, one that the AWQ build was calibrated on. The batch-1 timings predate current engine releases, AMD and Intel Gaudi have no timing in this band at all, and FP4 has none against BF16. The timings that do exist follow one rule. Decoding a small batch is limited by memory bandwidth, so 4-bit weights roughly double speed (2.12x for Qwen2.5-14B on an A100), but the gain vanishes once a large batch makes the GPU compute-bound (1.02x for Gemma 3 12B at batch size 256), where FP8 is the recipe that can still help. Many published accuracy deltas, including every HumanEval delta, lie within benchmark sampling noise. We close with a seven-item reporting checklist for future measurements.

AI.brief_summary: 该文汇总并核查 9B–20B 开源 LLM 量化部署的公开测速与精度数据，指出两者往往分开报告、条件不可比，并给出七项测量报告清单；其结论是 4-bit 权重在小 batch 解码时约 2 倍加速，大 batch 转为计算受限后收益消失，而不少精度差值落在采样噪声内。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「加速依赖内存带宽还是计算受限」「小幅精度差常不可区分于噪声」的测量视角，可能为 LVR 中动态计算的实际成本核算与效应量判定提供可供核查的线索，但本身不涉及视觉推理状态或证据使用。
